8.  American  Recovery Plan Act-  City Manager Russi reported on the American Recovery
  Essential Worker Premium Pay  Worker Premium Pay Stipends.  He stated that at the December Council
  Stipends  meeting, the City Council was presented with an outline of the City' s allocation
  of American Rescue Plan Act( ARPA) funds and a preliminary plan for their
  use. In addition to giving concurrence to the proposed uses, the City Council
  directed staff to bring back an outline of a Stipend for employees for their
  consideration. After researching the provisions of the Act and what other
  agencies are providing, staff has prepared a set of criteria that was reviewed
  by the City Council at their January 18 meeting. That plan was shared with the
  affected employees and their associations. In order to implement the stipends,
  final approval by City Council is necessary.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There was public comment. To hear what was said during public comment,
  please visit the City' s website to view the archived Council meeting.

  City Manager Russi responded to questions asked during public comment.
  Mayor Hepburn agreed  with  the Essential Worker Premium  Pay Stipends.  He

  stated that the City employees do an amazing job and it was important to show
  them appreciation for the tough job they do.

  Council Member Carder stated that the City employees are the backbone of
  the City. She stated it was a scary time during the pandemic especially for first
  responders.  She praised the public works staff for their work for providing
  street barricades to the downtown local businesses and restaurants during the
  pandemic  helping them to thrive. She also praised all the City employees who
  came in to work every day during the pandemic to keep the City running and
  for doing a great job.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis agreed with Council Member Carder. He stated that
  consideration and decisions were made for the use of the ARPA funds for the
  community, like the Small Businesses Grant Program, Housing Rehabilitation
  Grant Program and the funding of CIP improvement projects for the next five
  years. He stated that City employees serve the community and they are very
  much  appreciated.

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried to
  authorize staff to execute side letters with represented employee groups; to
  appropriate $ 520, 000 from the City' s ARPA allocation; and authorized the

  Finance Department to issue stipends as provided under the outlined criteria.
